key_evidence: The published 60.9 rests on a vector byte-identical to The Hartford, Travelers and MetLife at adjacent ranks 43, 50, 51 and 52. It is the 60.9 uniform-seed cluster, not a measurement. last_assessed was null and APPLIED_CHANGES.md has no Unum entry.

On 2025-04-17 the federal district court for the Eastern District of Tennessee granted final approval of a $14.8 million wage-and-hour class settlement. The class were Unum disability benefits specialists - the staff who process short- and long-term disability claims - who alleged exempt misclassification and unpaid overtime. About 910 participating class members averaged over $10,000 each, with 52 receiving more than $30,000.

That finding is the sharpest in the assessment: a disability insurer, by court-approved settlement, underpaid the very staff who decide whether disabled people get paid. I3 Internal Consistency scores 2/5 on adjudicated rather than alleged evidence.

Historical context, explicitly NOT scored as current conduct: the 2004 multistate settlement with 48 states required a $15 million fine, restructured claims procedures and reassessment of roughly 200,000 claims. It supports AB2, AB4, AB5 and EQ5 at 3/5 - real corrections and real money, but always compelled. The 45%-reversal and $558 million figures come from claimant-side advocacy sources (tier 1-2) and are NOT used as scoring anchors.

Ongoing ERISA denial litigation through 2025-2026 (fibromyalgia, chronic fatigue syndrome, mental health, back injury) with mixed outcomes including at least one appellate decision upholding a denial. Unresolved or defence-favourable litigation is NOT scored as a finding of harm; its volume is context only.

Genuine strength preserved: vocational rehabilitation and return-to-work are explicitly designed to restore earning capacity and end the claim, scoring B2 Autonomy Preservation at 4/5 - the highest single subdimension in the assessment.

evidence.claim: On 2025-04-17 the E.D. Tenn. granted final approval of a $14.8 million wage-and-hour class settlement covering Unum disability benefits specialists who alleged they were misclassified as exempt and denied overtime; about 910 participating class members averaged over $10,000 each.
evidence.source: McGillivary Steele Elkin LLP, reporting the court order

evidence.claim: Unum and its workers agreed a $14.8 million settlement to end the wage suit.

In 2004, 48 states settled with Unum, requiring a $15 million fine, restructured claims procedures and reassessment of roughly 200,000 disability claims, with California imposing a separate $8 million fine. Historical context only; claimant-side source, treated as indicative and not as a scoring anchor.

Courts continued hearing Unum long-term disability denial challenges through 2025 and into 2026 for fibromyalgia, chronic fatigue syndrome, depression and back injuries, with mixed outcomes. Recorded as context; not scored as a finding.
Unum Group’s FY2025 annual report (SEC Form ARS) discloses litigation and reserve development, supporting AB3 Transparency at 3/5.

notes: Rotation-sourced first evidence-based baseline; no in-window news event. Screening rule 3 does not constrain direction for a rotation entity, and the located evidence points down. Classified as SEED-BASELINE-RECALIBRATION plus one adjudicated 2025 conduct item, the same category as Cerebras Systems (2026-08-20). Most of the -21.5 is replacement of a placeholder that asserted anchor-4 behaviour (community-confirmed care, disparities investigated, acknowledgment prior to investigation) for which no evidence exists. Calibration flag recorded separately and NOT used to justify this move: The Hartford, Travelers and MetLife carry the identical 60.9 seed vector, none of them is moved here, and the plateau needs band-wide review. Evidence gap: Unum’s own sustainability and social-impact report was not retrieved in full, so AB3, AC3, S2 and I2 may be understated.
